amendments.because: Owner: every feature is proven for new and existing clients
amendments.done_when: A 'forge fasttest <base>' command works in any pytest repo without installing Forge into the project: Forge picks the changed test files, test files named after a changed module, and test files importing or mentioning it, then runs the repo's own test command from forge.toml narrowed to those files in the repo's environment, runs the full test command when conftest.py, pyproject.toml or a lock file changed, and caps pytest at half the machine's cores; no pytest plugin. Forge's own forge.toml and the skill use 'forge fasttest {base}'; doctor reports a fast_test that still says 'python -m forge.fasttest' with the one-line replacement. New repos: setup proposes it for pytest repos. Existing repos: get the command on upgrade; their forge.toml is never rewritten. One command-level test in a plain pytest repo without Forge installed in its environment.

Forge's own forge.toml and the skill use 'forge fasttest {base}'; doctor reports a fast_test that still says 'python -m forge.fasttest' with the one-line replacement. Command-level tests cover both kinds of client: a new client (forge init in a plain pytest repo, Forge not installed in its environment) whose proposed fast_test runs only the related tests at close; and an existing client adopted on an earlier release whose forge.toml carries the old 'python -m forge.fasttest' line, where doctor names the replacement, forge.toml is not rewritten, and after the owner's one-line change close runs only the related tests.

findings.body: The previously reported command-rewriting defect remains. For `python -m pip install pytest && python -m pytest tests`, both `pytest` tokens receive `--ignore` arguments, so pip fails before the tests run. The fallback at line 80 also appends pytest arguments to Ruff in `python run_tests.py && ruff check .`, even when the launcher forwards arguments correctly. Identify the actual pytest invocation or launcher before modifying its arguments, preserving the other shell commands.
findings.title: Recognize pytest invocations before adding pytest arguments

findings.body: This still merges addopts from every configuration candidate, including defaults when `-c` selects another file. An active pytest.ini without xdist settings and an inactive tox.ini containing `addopts = -n auto` cause Forge to inject `--maxprocesses`; without xdist installed, the otherwise valid test command fails with an unrecognized argument. [Pytest selects one configuration rather than merging candidates](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference/customize.html). Derive worker settings only from the configuration pytest actually selects.
findings.title: Read worker options only from pytest's selected configuration

findings.body: Explicit unrelated targets are removed only from the forge.toml command string. A target such as `tests/test_unrelated.py::test_unrelated` supplied through configuration addopts or PYTEST_ADDOPTS remains present despite the appended `--ignore`. [Pytest bypasses ignore checks for explicitly supplied paths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytest-dev/pytest/9.1.1/src/_pytest/main.py), so the picker can print only related files while still running unrelated tests. Filter explicit targets from both option sources while preserving their other settings.
findings.title: Exclude unrelated paths supplied through pytest addopts

findings.body: The updated setup paragraph still instructs the agent to use “the repo's Python runner with Forge installed” at line 302. The same instruction remains in both checked-in Forge skills. This contradicts the fix's installation-free client setup and can direct agents to add Forge to the client's environment unnecessarily. Clarify that the project runner belongs in the full test command and that the picker runs through the separately installed Forge tool.
findings.title: Remove the project-install instruction from setup guidance

why: The shipped Python test picker (uv run python -m forge.fasttest) fails in client repos with 'No module named forge', because Forge is a separate tool, not a dependency of the client's project; it only works in Forge's own repo
